unmet_requirements.requirement: every view must prove fit with a pinned 77x47 dump that shows the whole graph and no overflow banner
unmet_requirements.unmet: v2 (80x24: 3 columns over), v4 (34x48: 1 row over)
unmet_requirements.structural_finding: In `tb` this build spends 8 rows per rank (5 ranks = 40 rows, 6 ranks = 48 rows), so a 77x47 view holds at most five ranks. v4 needs six ranks because the Wi-Fi path reaches the gateway one hop before the WAN chain starts (wlp -> rtr -> ont -> vzagg -> vzbb -> cf). v2 needs two nodes in one rank for the host's parallel uplinks, and a two-node rank with two gap labels in this engine is about 80 columns wide (its three checked candidates measured 82, 80 and 80).
unmet_requirements.reshuffle_checked_and_rejected: Moving e10 (wlp -> rtr) from v4 into v3 would leave v4 a five-rank chain, but v3 would then hold a two-node rank (bond0 plus wlp) with two gap labels, which is the same geometry that put v2 at 80 columns — the breakage would move, not disappear. The genuinely clean fix is a fifth view splitting the WAN chain at vzagg, and the round caps the case at four views.
unmet_requirements.no_rule_broken: Neither relation nor label was deleted to reach the target: candidate v4-a1 (31x40, fits 47 rows) would have dropped e10 and was rejected for exactly that reason.
